source_note: Topic structure follows the Edexcel GCSE Design & Technology specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

connections.why: Knowing what new technologies do is needed to critically evaluate them
New technologies drive developments in energy generation and storage
Modern and smart materials are products of new and emerging technology
Mechanical and electronic systems are combined to give products functionality
Programmable components add controllable behaviour to electronic systems
Core material knowledge underpins specialist study of one category
A material's properties relate to its origin and available stock forms
Properties determine which shaping and forming processes can be used
Shaped components are then joined and finished to complete a product
The chosen process depends on the scale of production required
Real contexts surface the environmental, social and economic challenges to solve
Studying existing designers shows how others addressed similar challenges
Insights from others inform the strategies used to generate ideas
Generated ideas must be recorded and communicated clearly
The contextual challenge frames the NEA investigation
Research and the specification drive the generation of design ideas
Drawing and modelling skills are applied throughout the NEA design stage
A developed final design is then manufactured as a prototype
Specialist processes are applied when making the NEA prototype
The finished prototype is tested and evaluated against the brief
Quality control and tolerances guide accurate manufacture
Material choice is justified within the design proposals
